target.name: Atomic Industries
target.founder: Aaron Slodov, Austin Bishop, Lou Young Jr

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $25M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Atomic Industries, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Aaron Slodov, Austin Bishop, and Lou Young Jr., is evaluated against a comp universe of 9 private and 1 public company operating in the same sector. The company has raised $25M+ to date.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, anchoring to the $25M total raised as a baseline proxy, yielding $50M. Peer-median analysis examines four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: Generalist AI ($2.0B, Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B, Seed). This peer set produces a median valuation of $1.7B with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B. The large divergence between methods reflects the maturity gap between early-stage capital raised and later-stage peer valuations.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $42.5M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $875M. The substantial width of this range—spanning two orders of magnitude—underscores material uncertainty around whether Atomic will achieve comparable scale and exit multiples to the Series B+ peer set. Stage progression suggests a near-term floor; peer comps indicate potential ceiling. Key variables determining outcome include technology differentiation, customer traction, and capital efficiency relative to Robotics & Manufacturing precedents.
